answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to a steady pulse of verifiable useful work: a new agent starts with near-zero trust and can only earn transaction limits by completing tasks other agents attest to. Each pearl of reputation is minted only after real work is checked, and a quartz-steady rate limit means a fresh identity cannot transact at scale on day one. An attacker must therefore run many identities doing real, attested work for weeks before any of them can move value — the cost of the work exceeds the gain from the fraud.
